teaser.text: Alimentation Couche-Tard runs stores and fuel stations where people quickly buy something for themselves and something for their vehicle. Its business earns money from fuel, convenience goods, prepared food and services, then spends that money on products, people, property and financing.

blocks.heading: Where could Alimentation Couche-Tard Inc.'s shares go?

paragraphs.text: The forecast’s central outcome is modest appreciation, but the possible range remains wide. The weighted price is C$75.96 in October 2027, C$81.58 in October 2028 and C$89.81 in October 2029, equivalent to returns including dividends of negative 2%, positive 6% and positive 18%. The 2029 outcomes range from C$50.44 in the bear case to C$130.19 in the bull case, against today’s C$78.64.

blocks.heading: What could make Alimentation Couche-Tard Inc.'s shares rise or fall?

paragraphs.text: The bear case requires weaker fuel demand, lower fuel margins and acquisition financing to overwhelm merchandise and food growth. Żabka absorbs cash, buybacks remain limited and the valuation contracts. That produces C$61.06 in October 2027 and C$50.44 in October 2029, with a 25% probability. Falling comparable fuel volumes, volatile margins and the undisclosed Irving Oil purchase terms make this a material risk, but Couche-Tard’s regional diversification and dividend stability keep it from being central.

The bull case requires several successes at once. Foodservice and merchandise profit offset softer fuel volumes; distribution improves availability and lowers costs; Żabka integrates on schedule; debt falls and buybacks resume. The P/E then rises as investors gain evidence that returns are repeatable. The result is C$90.72 in October 2027 and C$130.19 in October 2029, with a 20% probability. The upside is substantial, but distribution payback and acquisition-by-acquisition returns remain unproven.

blocks.heading: How much does Alimentation Couche-Tard Inc. pay per share?

paragraphs.text: Dividends rise in the base case from US$0.66 to US$0.80 per share, using roughly 10% annual growth from the latest annualized rate of about US$0.60. That is below the prior five-year growth rate, but fiscal 2026 dividends used only about one fifth of free cash flow. The bear case holds dividends at US$0.60 because debt and investment take priority. The bull case reaches US$0.92 on 15% annual growth, requiring stronger cash earnings and acquisition synergies.

blocks.heading: What has Alimentation Couche-Tard Inc. guided for the year?

paragraphs.text: On February 11, 2026, Couche-Tard introduced Core + More, replacing its earlier outlook. “Core” means improving the businesses it already knows; “More” means adding growth opportunities and the capabilities to support them. Through fiscal 2030, management targets annualized adjusted EBITDA growth of 6.0%–8.0% and adjusted earnings-per-share growth of at least 10.0%, excluding major transactions.

The operating targets are comparable-store merchandise growth of 2%–3%, total merchandise and service revenue growth of 4%–5%, fuel gross profit growth with inflation, and normalized expenses at inflation or below. Comparable-store growth shows whether established locations are improving, rather than letting new stores do all the work.

blocks.heading: Has Alimentation Couche-Tard Inc. kept its past promises?

paragraphs.text: Promises also need exact definitions. In March 2026, Alex Miller said the company was on track to build 100 new stores by fiscal year-end. The annual report later described 130 sites added or improved, including relocations and rebuilds. Those categories are not interchangeable, so the larger figure does not alone prove the new-build promise was met.
